answer: Make every agent open a sonnet vault at the wharf before it works. It locks a refundable deposit inside and seals a short original sonnet to its own job, a text no other agent has used. Peers at the wharf check each sonnet against the vault ledger, so a copied one flags its owner. Clean work releases part of the deposit and unlocks larger jobs, while fake work slashes the deposit and burns the record. Assume a fake costs $6,000, about $6 million per 1,000 fakes, so a flood costs more than it earns. Like a wharf that only berths ships with their own papers, the vault keeps fakes out.
